### Software as a Differentiator
Software accelerates value delivery across industries (e.g., banks trading securely, retailers offering seamless experiences, government serving efficiently). James Bessen (2017) found tech explains revenue/productivity gains more than M&A and entrepreneurship; McAfee and Brynjolfsson (2008) linked tech to profitability. DevOps emerged to solve the wicked problem of building secure, resilient, rapidly evolving distributed systems at scale. Successful adopters include Netflix, Amazon, Google, Facebook, Capital One, Target, and the US Federal Government’s Technology Transformation Service and US Digital Service.

### Industry Progress and Disconnects
Forrester (Stroud et al. 2017) found 31% of the industry lacks necessary practices (continuous integration/delivery, Lean, collaborative culture). Gartner (Panetta 2017) reported 47% of CEOs face board pressure to digitally transform. Forrester (Klavens et al. 2017) noted organizations overestimate DevOps progress, with executives overestimating more than practitioners. This disconnect means potential value is greater than leaders realize, necessitating accurate measurement and communication to inform strategy.

### Capabilities vs. Maturity Models
Organizations must focus on capabilities, not maturity models, for four reasons:
1. Maturity models imply an endpoint ("done"); capability models drive continuous improvement.
2. Maturity models are linear/lock-step; capability models are multidimensional/dynamic, allowing customized approaches based on team context, systems, and constraints.
3. Maturity models measure tooling install bases (vanity metrics); capability models are outcome-based, identifying levers that drive key outcomes.
4. Maturity models are static; capability models adapt to ever-changing landscapes where "high-performing" standards shift yearly.

### Evidence-Based Performance Drivers
Non-predictors of performance include application age/technology (mainframe "systems of record" vs. greenfield "systems of engagement"), whether ops or dev deploys, and implementing a change approval board (CAB). Instead, 24 key capabilities drive software delivery and organizational performance.

### High Performer Metrics (2017)
Compared to low performers, high performers achieved: 46x more frequent code deployments, 440x faster lead time from commit to deploy, 170x faster mean time to recover (MTTR), and 5x lower change failure rate. Compared to 2016, the tempo gap narrowed but the stability gap widened. Low performers likely increased tempo without investing in quality, causing larger failures. High performers build quality in, achieving both speed and stability without trade-offs.
